issues.description: The UML in the problem statement specifies Ride.abbreviation as type 'char', but the solution's Ride class declares abbreviation as a String. This contradicts the UML specification and will confuse students about the expected type for the abbreviation attribute and its getter.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the code with the UML: change the Ride.abbreviation attribute and its getter to type 'char' (update the field declaration, constructor parameter and getter return type). Alternatively, if String is intended, update the UML and problem statement to specify String for abbreviation. Prefer changing Ride to use 'char' to match the UML and tasks.

issues.description: RollerCoaster's constructor in the solution declares a 'char abbreviation' parameter but calls super(name, abbreviation) where Ride's constructor expects a String abbreviation. This parameter/type mismatch between subclass constructor and superclass constructor will cause a compile error and contradicts the intended UML type for abbreviation.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure constructor parameter types match the superclass: either change RollerCoaster's constructor to accept a String abbreviation (and update UML if needed) or change Ride to use a char abbreviation so the subclass can pass the char through. To conform with the UML, update Ride to use 'char' for abbreviation and update its constructor accordingly so super(name, abbreviation) is valid.
